- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 3 forecast values before adjusting for sentiment direction.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model often fails to capture momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average: 60% recent price, 40% sentiment-adjusted trend.
